references.text: The same warning to let the people go is given earlier in the chapter, showing Pharaoh's repeated demand.
God's command to let the people go to worship him in the wilderness, which is the basis for all the plagues.
A similar formulation of the warning before the plague on livestock, with the same condition to let the people go.
The warning about the locust plague uses similar language about them filling the houses, just as the flies do here.
The psalmist recalls the fly plague (עָרֹב) that God sent upon Egypt as part of his mighty deeds.
A reference to how God spoke and a swarm of flies (עָרֹב) came over all the land of Egypt.
The fulfillment of this warning, where the flies actually come upon Egypt.
Parallel descriptions of plagues invading the private space of Pharaoh and his servants.
A direct narrative and linguistic parallel in the threat of plagues if they refuse.
Contrasting actions (invasion versus withdrawal) with an identical list of affected parties.
A direct narrative continuation with the same conditional structure and a threat of another plague.
A direct narrative follow-up showing the promise that the plagues will be withdrawn upon obedience.
